clue.text: So-called 'dear' runs off after six-footer

indicators.note: the eloping comes after the insect in the answer

parts.note: an insect has six legs, so an ant is a six-footer
elopes means runs off secretly to marry

explanation.surface: A lover who calls someone 'dear' runs off with them after a very tall partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' in quotes is a pun on deer: antelopes are often loosely taken for deer, hence 'so-called'.
explanation.definitionFit: Antelopes are horned grazing animals often mistaken for deer, which sounds like the clue's quoted word.

clue.text: Neither obtuse nor grave (and not right)

definitions.text: Neither obtuse nor grave (and not right)

parts.words: Neither obtuse nor grave (and not right)
parts.note: an angle that is neither obtuse nor right, and an accent that is not grave

explanation.walkthrough: Two vocabularies meet: angles are obtuse, right or the answer; French accents are grave or the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle under ninety degrees is neither obtuse nor right, and the accent paired against the grave shares the same name.

clue.text: Eat nuts struggling, suffering from this?

definitions.text: Eat nuts struggling, suffering from this?

indicators.note: letters that are struggling are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tries to eat nuts but cannot, because their jaw is locked.
explanation.walkthrough: The disease is also called lockjaw, which is why a sufferer would struggle to eat nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: This bacterial infection causes muscle spasms, notably lockjaw, making chewing a struggle.

clue.text: No pressure to satisfy contract

indicators.note: no means the letter for pressure is dropped from the word

parts.note: to please someone is to satisfy them

explanation.surface: A relaxed deal: no pressure is needed to meet the terms of the contract.
explanation.definitionFit: A lease is a legal contract letting property for a set term.

clue.text: Grabs pawn in unfinished game

parts.note: P is the chess notation for a pawn

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the game is cut off

parts.note: chess is the game

explanation.surface: A player snatches a pawn during a chess game they never finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinch is to grab or steal, so pinches means grabs.

clue.text: Well, what to do with crumbling mortar is a painful subject

parts.note: so and well are both sentence openers

parts.words: what to do with crumbling mortar
parts.note: brickwork with crumbling mortar needs to be repointed

explanation.surface: A builder's view on fixing crumbling mortar turns out to be a touchy topic.
explanation.walkthrough: To repoint is to replace the mortar between bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: A sore point is a subject that causes hurt or annoyance when raised.

clue.text: Liquid lunch perhaps very revolting

parts.note: so can mean very, as in so good
a people up in arms are revolting, so up means in revolt

explanation.surface: A liquid lunch, presumably boozy, sounds quite disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquid lunch' usually means drinks; here it is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Soup is food you drink, so it is literally a liquid lunch, as an example.

clue.text: Being from the north, leaving clubs stupefied by drink

indicators.note: leaving means the card suit letter departs from the word

parts.note: Scotland is the north of Britain, so being from there is Scottish

explanation.surface: A northerner leaves the golf club in a drunken haze.
explanation.definitionFit: Sottish describes a sot, someone habitually befuddled with alcohol.

clue.text: Get off the phone!

parts.note: read as removing an app or program from a mobile device

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation sounds like a demand to end a call, but it means removing software from the handset.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove software from a device such as a smartphone is the computing sense of the word.

clue.text: Antiquary wasting a year translating verse

indicators.note: translating moves the remaining letters into a new form
wasting means the year letter is lost from the word

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A collector of old things squanders a year turning poetry into another language.
explanation.definitionFit: A quatrain is a stanza of four lines, a unit of verse.

clue.text: Return afterwards, holding one to sell

indicators.note: holding means the outer letters keep the numeral inside
return means the word is turned to run backwards

parts.note: later means afterwards
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A shop advises coming back later, keeping one item aside to sell.
explanation.definitionFit: To retail is to sell goods to the public in small quantities.

clue.text: One hopes people will come late to this meeting

definitions.text: One hopes people will come late to this meeting

parts.words: One hopes people will come late to this meeting
parts.note: 'the late' are the dead, whom a medium hopes will come to the gathering

explanation.walkthrough: 'Come late' reads as poor punctuality, but late here means deceased: spirits are summoned at such a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A seance is a gathering at which people try to contact the spirits of the dead.

clue.text: Rewritten epitaphs are most favourable

indicators.note: rewritten means the letters of the word are set out afresh

explanation.surface: Gravestone inscriptions, once revised, are the most flattering.
explanation.definitionFit: Happiest can mean most fortunate or apt, as in the happiest choice.

clue.text: School uniform switched to vulgar stuff

indicators.note: switched means the two parts swap places from their clue order

parts.note: a team's kit is its uniform
SCH is the standard dictionary abbreviation for school

explanation.surface: A school changes its uniform for something tacky.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch is art or decoration considered tasteless and garish.

clue.text: I trade house that's featured in exhibition

definitions.note: the answer is the name that features in the Ideal Home Exhibition

parts.note: to deal is to trade
a home is a house

explanation.surface: An estate agent swaps a property shown at a fair.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ideal Home Exhibition (now Show) is a long-running London fair of homes and household goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's annual Ideal Home Exhibition carries these two words in its title, showing off model houses.

clue.text: Go for drinking session and almost score

definitions.meaning: first meaning: head to the pub to drink
second meaning: in football, strike the crossbar and narrowly miss a goal

explanation.walkthrough: The bar is both the pub counter and the crossbar of the goal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means going out drinking, and in sport striking the goal frame without scoring.

clue.text: Tough woman keeps family notice

indicators.note: keeps means the pronoun holds the relatives within it

parts.note: she refers to a woman
kin are family
an ad is a notice

explanation.surface: A formidable woman holds on to the family announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: Tough here is a noun, a thug, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough is a rough, aggressive person, and a skinhead is a youth from a shaven-headed, often violent subculture.

clue.text: Get comfortable again on bench

parts.note: re means on, about
a settle is a wooden bench with a high back

explanation.surface: Someone sits back down on a bench to get comfy once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To resettle is to settle down once more, making oneself at ease again.

clue.text: Always a heavyweight team now in trouble?

parts.note: ever means always
a ton is a heavy weight

explanation.surface: A club that has always been a big name now faces difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is a Liverpool football club, which was fighting relegation when this appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is a Premier League football side, then struggling near the foot of the table.

clue.text: In danger perhaps, no longer maintaining position

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
a model posed by holding a position

explanation.surface: Someone stayed still in a pose, but is no longer safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposed means unprotected and open to harm, one kind of danger.

clue.text: Get to grips with rigging

definitions.meaning: first meaning: deal with, take on
second meaning: a ship's ropes and pulleys

explanation.walkthrough: 'Get to grips with rigging' reads like a sailor's task, but it splits into two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle a problem is to deal with it, and tackle is also a vessel's ropes and blocks.

clue.text: Fine fabric needs about inch off

indicators.note: about means the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A delicate material needs trimming by about an inch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'approximately'; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiffon is a light, sheer silk or nylon material.

clue.text: Waste gambling token, which should have been a good investment

parts.note: to blue money is to squander it
a chip is a casino token

explanation.surface: A gambler regrets squandering a casino chip that ought to have been a sound bet.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue as a verb meaning squander is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-chip shares are those of large, reliable companies, seen as a safe investment.

clue.text: Miss musical as I enter into clinic

definitions.note: the musical is Miss Saigon, so the answer completes its title

indicators.note: into means the pieces are placed inside the clinic

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium
to go in is to enter

explanation.surface: A woman skips a show as she checks into a clinic.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss Saigon is the stage show by the Les Miserables team, set in the Vietnamese city.

clue.text: Small implement to make low seat

parts.note: a tool is an implement

explanation.surface: A little tool is used to build a low seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A stool is a backless seat, often low.

clue.text: It may be nestling in the barn

definitions.text: It may be nestling in the barn

parts.words: It may be nestling in the barn
parts.note: a nestling is a baby bird, here a young barn owl

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nestling' reads as a verb, snuggling down, but it is the noun for a chick.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a young owl, and barn owls nest in barns.

clue.text: A warm bath — to an excess in the centre …

indicators.note: in means the excess sits inside the centre

parts.note: a hub is a centre
OTT is over the top, excessive

explanation.surface: A warm bath is too much in the middle of things.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot tub is a large heated outdoor bath for several people.

clue.text: … and a cold shower

parts.note: a shower of cold flakes, following the warm bath of the previous clue

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the warm bath above, so 'cold shower' looks like bathing; it is weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall of snow is a shower of frozen precipitation, cold weather from the sky.

clue.text: Martin is college head

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... Martin, the American singer
second meaning: the head of some colleges

explanation.walkthrough: Martin is a surname here; the answer is the singer's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Dean Martin was a famous crooner, and a dean leads a college or faculty.

clue.text: Our neighbour Peter worked with land

indicators.note: worked means the letters are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: The neighbour Peter farmed the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars, called this for its rusty colour, is Earth's neighbouring planet.
